sections.overview: Libellula axilena Westwood, 1837 is a North American dragonfly in the skimmer family Libellulidae.
sections.identification: A dark bar between the nodus and stigma on each wing gives it its common name; males and females differ in appearance.
sections.habitat: It frequents ponds, swamp pools and other still waters near forests, including temporary pools in cleared utility corridors.
sections.diet: Adults forage near forest edges, but the consulted species account does not identify particular prey.
sections.behavior: Males perch on exposed twigs beside water and patrol back and forth over pools; adults often forage along forest edges.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific details of courtship, egg laying and larval development are sparse in the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: The slaty skimmer (L. incesta) is a similar relative, but dark wing bars help separate L. axilena; the Great Blue Skimmer (L. vibrans) is another close look-alike noted in regional identification guides.
sections.conservation: The North Carolina species account lists a global conservation rank of G5, while noting that abundance varies across the state.
